title: Didn't last longer than a month but customer service saved it
text:
I bought this device based on a lot of positive reviews and for the first three weeks, it performed exactly as advertised. The setup was intuitive, the build quality felt solid, and it integrated perfectly with my other home electronics. I was genuinely impressed with the performance and thought I had found a great deal.

However, just as I hit the one-month mark, the unit suddenly stopped powering on. I tried every troubleshooting step in the manual, checked the cables, and attempted a hard reset, but nothing worked. It was incredibly frustrating to have a piece of tech fail so quickly, especially when it had been working flawlessly up until that point. I was convinced I had just bought a lemon and was prepared to leave a one-star review and demand a full refund.

That is where the experience changed. I reached out to their customer service team via email, and I was surprised by how quickly they responded. Unlike many electronics companies that make you jump through endless hoops or try to convince you that the failure is your fault, they were professional and efficient. They acknowledged the issue immediately and, without making me go through a lengthy return process for the broken unit, they shipped me a brand-new replacement via expedited shipping.

The new unit arrived within three days and is currently working perfectly. While I am still slightly concerned about the long-term reliability since the first one died so fast, the way the company handled the situation completely saved the experience for me. It is rare to find a company that actually stands behind its warranty and values the customer's time.

I am giving this four stars instead of five because a product shouldn't fail within thirty days, regardless of how good the support is. But because the replacement process was seamless and the product itself is great when it works, I would still recommend it to others. Just make sure to keep your receipt and contact their support if you run into any glitches.

title: Nice Cabinet and Board, BAD Darts
text:
I bought this dart cabinet and board set a few weeks ago because I wanted a neat, all-in-one option for occasional games in the garage. First impressions were positive: the cabinet itself looks good, is solidly built, and the magnetic closures keep it tidy when not in use. The finish is nice and it mounted easily to the wall — overall it gives a more polished look than a cheap foam board hung with screws.

Unfortunately, the darts and the board are where this product falls apart. The board surface is a cheap sisal substitute that wears unevenly and already shows fraying around the triple 20 after only a handful of sessions. More noticeably, the included darts feel very low quality. The shafts are flimsy plastic that bent or loosened almost every game, and the threads that attach to the flights stripped easily. I tried tightening them and replacing flights, but they didn’t hold alignment and the darts wobbled a lot in flight, which made accurate throws nearly impossible.

The scoring ring on the board is thin metal and seems okay for stopping bounce-outs, but the combination of soft board material and poor darts resulted in a higher-than-expected rate of bounced or dropped darts — not fun when you’re keeping score. I would have been happier if the set included at least mid-range darts or allowed for easy upgrades; swapping in better darts helps, but doesn’t solve the fact that the board itself degrades quickly.

If you want a sharp-looking cabinet and a basic board for casual display and very light play, this will do the job. If you’re buying it to play regularly or expect decent dart performance out of the box, you’ll be disappointed and likely need to buy replacement darts (and possibly a better board) soon after. Hence the middle-of-the-road rating.

title: MacBook Air M1: Cracking on corners after a few months.
text: I was genuinely excited to upgrade to the new MacBook Air M1, anticipating the promise of a lightweight, powerful, and durable machine for my daily workflow. Unfortunately, my experience has been nothing short of disappointing, particularly regarding the build quality. After only three months of careful, normal use, I noticed small but noticeable cracks appearing on both bottom corners of the chassis. This is not a result of any drops or impacts; the laptop sat securely in my bag, which is lined with protective padding, yet the aluminum casing simply gave way under minimal stress. It seems the structural integrity of the bottom case is severely compromised, making this device far less robust than its predecessor or even other laptops in this price range. For a product that costs over a thousand dollars, I expected a level of durability that withstands everyday commuting and handling without falling apart. I have since contacted Apple Support, but the repair process is tedious and the incident feels like a design flaw rather than a random manufacturing defect. It is frustrating to invest in premium hardware only to watch it deteriorate so quickly. I cannot recommend this model to anyone who values longevity or build quality. If you are looking for a reliable machine that won’t show signs of wear and tear in just a few months, I would strongly advise looking elsewhere. The performance is fine, but the physical durability is unacceptable for the price point.

title: Easy Vegetable Dishes for Even Your Picky Eater
text:
From the Book's description:

Everyone knows that vegetables are healthy and a necessary part of our daily diet. But not everyone knows just how delicious they can be. Sensational Vegetable Recipes shows you how to make great main meals from vegetables, as well as side dishes and delectable snacks. There's also a chapter on quick one-step ways to cook ten of the most popular vegetables. The clear step-by-step photographs guide you through each of the recipes, clearly explaining techniques that may be new to you. And there is practical advice on buying, storing and preparing vegetables, and ideas to let you take advantage of the great range of fresh and packaged produce available in markets today.

My Review:

I bought this book at my local Borders store in the bargain/clearance section years ago. What caught my attention was the bright colored vegetable dishes and the claim of step-by-step. Since then, I"ve made many of the recipes, including a family favorite "Savory Fennel Crumble", easy side dishes such as "Warm tomato and herb salad", "Asparagus and snow pea salad", Main dishes like "Vegetable lasagna", "Vegetable Pie" and so on. I've even tried the sections on the most popular vegetables, carrots, onions and so on.

The recipes truly are easy, step-by-step, for anyone, from the novice home cook to the tried and true professional chef. Falling somewhere in between, I found the recipes easy, delicious and crowd-pleasing. I've taken them to pot-luck dinners where everyone wants to know the recipe! They are made with common, every day ingredients, easily found in your hometown grocery store, the steps are not complicated. You may even win over your family's picky eater!

I would recommend this vegetable cookbook to anyone looking for something fresh for the family dinner. Even though it is no longer in print, there should be copies floating around the internet and used book stores. Easily five stars.

I originally bought this item because I wanted to be better prepared for unexpected situations during my weekend hiking trips. I have always tried to pack light, but after a few close calls with bad weather and minor gear failures, I realized that having a reliable backup is more important than saving a few ounces of pack weight. The build quality is impressive. It feels rugged and durable, which is a necessity for anything categorized under sports and outdoors. It is compact enough to fit into a side pocket of my bag without taking up too much room, but it is substantial enough that I trust it to work when it actually matters.

What I appreciate most is the peace of mind it provides. There is a certain level of anxiety that comes with heading into the backcountry, and knowing I have this on hand for emergencies makes the experience much more enjoyable. It is one of those tools that you hope you never actually have to use in a dire situation, but you are incredibly grateful to have it when things go wrong.

The price point was very fair for the level of reliability offered. I have looked at several other options in this category, but this one felt the most dependable. Whether you are an experienced outdoorsman or someone who just goes for occasional walks in the woods, this is a smart investment. It arrived quickly and was packaged well. title: Very pleased- holds a lot
text:
I was pleasantly surprised by how much this organizer actually holds—and how well it fits into our kitchen space. I bought it to corral pantry overflow and to store small appliances and gadgets, and it has performed far beyond my expectations. The build feels sturdy and well-made; the shelves don’t wobble even when fully loaded, and the materials look like they will stand up to regular use. I appreciate the neutral finish that blends with my other kitchen items without drawing attention.

Assembly was straightforward. The instructions were clear, the hardware was all there, and it took me about 30–40 minutes to put together by myself. The pieces snapped together tightly and the final unit felt solid. No weird gaps or misaligned parts. It also came packaged nicely, with corners protected, so nothing was scratched or dented.

What sold me was the capacity. I can fit multiple cereal boxes, large baking mixes, and even my stand mixer on a lower shelf with room to spare. The adjustable shelving is a huge plus—I was able to customize the heights to store tall bottles and cereal boxes on one side and shorter items like spice tins and snack packs on another. There’s also a shallow top shelf that’s perfect for storing cutting boards and baking sheets vertically.

Cleaning is easy: a quick wipe down removes crumbs and dust. The open design allows good airflow, which helps keep things from smelling stale—something I noticed with our old enclosed pantry shelf. The unit doesn’t take up much floor space but adds a lot of usable storage, which is ideal for smaller kitchens or apartments.

A small note: if you’re planning to store very heavy items on the top shelf, I’d recommend anchoring it to the wall for peace of mind. Other than that, this organizer has made a noticeable difference in how tidy and accessible my kitchen supplies are. Great value for the price—functional, attractive, and robust. Highly recommended for anyone who needs extra storage without a major overhaul.

title: Seat is not cushiony
text:
I bought this chair because the listing promised “plush seating” and “all-day comfort,” but what arrived could not be further from that description. The seat is not cushiony at all — it’s hard and flat, with a thin foam layer that compresses immediately and leaves you feeling like you’re sitting on a board. After just 20–30 minutes I started shifting constantly trying to find a comfortable position. I’ve tried adding a seat pad and a small pillow, which helped marginally, but it defeats the purpose of buying a supposedly comfortable chair.

The upholstery feels cheap and slightly rough to the touch, not the soft fabric that the pictures suggested. The seams around the cushion area are already showing signs of stress where my weight concentrates, and I’m worried about long-term durability. Assembly was OK if you’re handy, but the parts didn’t feel sturdy and the frame creaked a little the first week I used it.

What bothered me most was the misleading product copy and photos. If the manufacturer had called this a minimalist dining chair with thin padding, I would have understood the lower cost. But advertising it as “plush” and “supportive” set expectations that were never met. For short visits it’s tolerable, but for working from home, long meals, or reading, it’s uncomfortable.

I’m returning it and looking for a chair with actual cushioning and better build quality. Save yourself the hassle and avoid this if comfort is important to you.

text:
I wish I could give this product zero stars because it genuinely disappointed me on multiple levels. I bought the "Thin" line of dietary supplements with high hopes, expecting a subtle, perhaps unnoticeable shift in my lifestyle that would lead to results. Instead, I found myself dealing with a product that felt more like a placebo with a premium price tag attached to it. From the moment I opened the bottle, the quality was questionable. The capsules had a strange, overly powdery texture that suggested poor manufacturing standards, which immediately put me on edge regarding the actual ingredients inside.

The marketing claims were aggressive, promising noticeable thinning of fat layers within weeks without rigorous exercise or dietary changes. Let me be clear: there was nothing noticeable. I followed the instructions precisely, taking the recommended dosage every single day for four weeks. During this time, I also monitored my caloric intake and maintained my usual activity levels, so any change should have been detectable. There was none. In fact, I felt slightly more bloated in the mornings, which was the opposite of the intended effect.

Customer service was equally frustrating. When I reached out to ask if this was normal, I received a generic, automated response that offered no real solution or explanation. It felt like they were just trying to silence a complaint rather than address a potential issue with the batch. I checked online forums and found several other users reporting the same lack of efficacy, which confirms that this isn’t just bad luck on my part.

The cost is another major factor. For the price of one bottle, I could have purchased a gym membership for two months or hired a nutritionist for a consultation. Those resources would have likely yielded better, healthier, and more sustainable results than this overhyped supplement. It is clear that the brand is spending more on advertising than on effective formulation. I do not recommend this to anyone looking for genuine health improvements. Save your money and invest in whole foods and physical activity instead. This product is a waste of cash and time, and I will not be repurchasing it under any circumstances.

This aesthetic alone was enough to make me confident that I was making a sensible investment in my daily routine. The product arrived quickly and was well-protected, which is always a relief when ordering fragile glass containers online.

Upon opening the bottle, the first thing I noticed was the scent. It has a very distinct, fresh aroma that reminds me slightly of citrus but with a subtle nutty undertone, likely from the apricot kernel oil mentioned on the label. It is not overpowering or perfumed in a way that feels artificial. Instead, it smells natural and inviting, which sets a pleasant tone for my morning skincare ritual. I have combination skin, which means I usually struggle to find a moisturizer that hydrates without making my T-zone look greasy by midday. This product has managed to strike a surprising balance.

The texture is lightweight and absorbs into the skin relatively quickly, leaving behind a soft, supple finish rather than a heavy, occlusive layer. I noticed a significant improvement in the dryness around my nose and cheeks, areas that usually flare up during colder months. My skin feels more resilient and less reactive to environmental changes. However, I am giving this product four stars instead of five for one specific reason. While the hydration is excellent, I found that for my oily zones, I might need to use a slightly lighter layer or perhaps pair it with a mattifying powder during the day to maintain shine control. It works well, but it requires a bit of adjustment depending on where you apply it on your face.

The ingredients list is transparent and reassuring, focusing on natural oils and gentle botanicals. I appreciate that there are no harsh sulfates or artificial fragrances cluttering the formula. For anyone looking for a straightforward, effective moisturizer that does exactly what it promises without unnecessary gimmicks, this is a strong contender. It is not a miracle worker that will erase years of sun damage overnight, but it is a reliable staple for maintaining healthy, hydrated skin. The price point is reasonable for the quality of the formula, and I expect to repurchase this once I finish the current bottle. By interweaving her own family history Ms. Chang talked about the idea of going out. Her grand father went out. Her father went out. title: Needed wheels
text:
I bought these replacement wheels because the original set on my cat’s rolling carrier started to squeak and wobble after a few years of use. I’d been putting off replacing them, but my carrier wouldn’t roll smoothly anymore and I was tired of careful maneuvering whenever I took my cat to the vet. Overall, these wheels did what I needed — so I’m giving four stars.

First, the fit was the most important part for me, and these matched the measurements listed in the description. Installation was straightforward: a little pop and snap into the socket, no tools required for the front caster wheels. The rear wheels needed a small screwdriver to remove a clip from the old set, but the package included clear instructions and a tiny plastic washer that made everything sit snugly. After swapping all four, the carrier rolled much more smoothly and quietly. No more loud scraping on tile or the awkward lurch when turning.

The materials feel decent for the price. The plastic is not super heavy-duty, but it’s sturdier than the flimsy wheels I had on the original carrier toward the end. They’ve handled a few months of regular use (weekly trips to the vet and occasional travel) without cracking or excessive wear. The bearings are adequate — not silky-smooth like higher-end casters, but good enough for a pet carrier that’s mostly moved short distances by hand.

That said, there are a couple of reasons I didn’t give five stars. One wheel arrived with a slight cosmetic scuff, and the axle housing on one piece felt a little looser than the others — it’s still worked fine but it gave me a moment of concern during installation. Also, the wheels don’t swivel quite as freely as the originals did, so turning on thick carpet still requires a bit of effort. If you have heavy or very active pets, or plan to pull the carrier over long distances, you might prefer a metal-bearing wheel or a branded replacement.

In summary: these wheels are a solid, affordable fix that saved me from buying a whole new carrier. They fit well, were easy to install, and restored smooth, quiet rolling for everyday use. A small quality-control improvement would make them perfect, but for the price they’re a practical and satisfactory replacement.

title: excellent read
text:
I rarely write reviews, but this book compelled me to share how much it exceeded my expectations. From the first chapter I was hooked — the pacing is just right, characters feel authentic, and the prose is both elegant and accessible. I found myself staying up later than I intended because I kept telling myself "just one more chapter," and then another.

What I appreciated most was how the author balanced plot momentum with quiet, character-driven moments. The relationships in the story are nuanced; nobody is purely heroic or villainous, and that complexity made the emotional beats land hard. There are lines I highlighted because they captured things I've felt but never quite been able to say. The book also manages to surprise without relying on cheap twists — the revelations arise naturally from the characters' choices, which made them satisfying and believable.

The themes felt timely without being preachy. Issues around identity, belonging, and forgiveness are woven into the narrative in a way that made me reflect on my own life long after I finished. The setting is vividly drawn; I could picture scenes clearly, and certain passages transported me to specific seasons and smells in a way that great novels do.

Formatting and editing were clean—no distracting typos—so my reading flow was uninterrupted. I'm recommending this to friends who like literary fiction with heart and readers who enjoy emotionally intelligent storytelling. If you're looking for a book that will stay with you, provoke thought, and make you care about its characters, this is an excellent read. I plan to keep a copy on my shelf and revisit it in the future.

title: The kind of book that you'll be reluctant to finish.
text:
Ever since the quality of Elizabeth George's books took a nosedive, I've been searching for another favorite mystery author. I've found her. And interestingly, like Ms. George, Deborah Crombie is an American woman who sets her mysteries in England.

The book has three threads: one is the ongoing romantic relationship between Superintendent Kincaid and his partner, Gemma James. A second is the mystery itself, involving a beautiful woman whose body is found carefully laid out in a park. The third is the genesis of the relationship among some of the characters/suspects and their families, a relationship which began back when English children were transported to the countryside to spare them the horrors of the World War II Blitz.

All three themes are handled beautifully. The characters of Duncan Kincaid and Gemma James continue to develop believably throughout this series. (This is, I believe, the sixth Kincaid/James book). The real-life problems and uncertainties they encounter while trying to maintain their family and professional obligations, and leave time for themselves and each other, will strike a believable chord with anyone old enough to have gone through this phase of life. The mystery is complex and unpredictable enough to be challenging but not confusing. The ending is beautiful - it settles both the mystery and the unresolved pain from the events of the 1940's.

If you haven't discovered the Crombie/Kincaid/James series yet, I recommend starting with the first one, "A Share in Death," which was nominated for an Agatha as best first novel of 1993. But I've read all of the first six, and they're all excellent.

title: Will to Power
text:
Reading Mr. Simmons' "Kiss and Make-Up," even the most churlish reader cannot but immediately grasp that he is the Baudelaire of his generation. Though never so despairing as his 19th century counterpart, Simmons nonetheless explores and exposes with refreshing candor the darkest impulses of the human spirit while affirming the life force of pure carnality.
While the less perceptive observer may dismiss Simmons' work as masturbatory egoism, it instead reveals the realization of Nietzsche's Ubermensch. Maligned and misunderstood, the true Nietzschean "Over-Man" rejects conventional behavioral norms and aspires to self-authentication, self-affirmation. This man is Gene Simmons - Bohemian visionary, fearless poet, nimble entrepreneur, and voracious lover of life and women.
Part Byronic hero and part Le Petomaine, Simmons, in "Kiss and Make-Up," offers the reader a glimpse of the redemptive power of debauchery.

title: Better respected than loved.
text:
"The Morels", a debut novel by Christopher Hacker, is one of those novels that can be described as better respected than loved. The story - a story within a story - is the tale of how a bunch of bad decisions have affected the lives of at least three generations of one family - the Morels - and those of people tangentially connected with them.

Arthur Morel, a musical prodigy, only child of divorced parents has walked through life in seeming non-connection with the realities we all have to deal with. After a particularly beautiful musical recital, the teenaged Arthur has performed an on-stage act of defilement that has stunned and revolted his audience. The years pass, Arthur has met, married a young woman called Penelope, and fathered a son, Will, with her. Penelope supports the family as a pastry chef while Arthur continues to "dabble" with life. He publishes a well-received novel and is in the process of finishing his second novel, called "The Morels", when Christopher Hacker's book begins. The story Hacker tells is narrated by a young man - himself adrift in movie making - who had known Arthur as the young defiler and now moves back into Arthur's life. He acts as teller of Arthur's story and its major interpreter.

"Interpreted" because there are a lot of actions which need to be interpreted to both those affected by the actions and those merely standing-by, observing. Are a man's possible incestuous thoughts always acted on - or can they merely remain, safely, thoughts? Where do lies and truth-telling become hopelessly meshed until neither is recognisable? In a broad way, Hacker's book is a bit like "The Dinner", by Herman Koch, another book where families and lies are tossed together and the truth never quite emerges.

Christopher Hacker's book should make the reader think about truth and lies and that muddy middle in between. Arthur, Penelope, and Will Morel are victims of both lies and truth, which they, themselves, perpetrate. It's an interesting book.

title: Recommend This Switch Box
text:
After several month's use on my HD flat panel TV, I can easily recommend this box if you need to "fan-out" a single HDMI input port to five independent signal sources. It does exactly what it says -- you control which input is selected, without the box trying to automatically switch to whichever input line is "active". The remote works well and the overall hook-up and operation is simple and straight forward. Overall device quality seemed very good and packaging for shipment was good. I could not detect any added audio or HD video signal deterioration/distortion. The instructions are fairly adequate, just remember to pull the plastic insulating tape out of the back of the remote to allow the battery to make internal electrical contact to start the remote! This was not mentioned in the instruction sheet of the unit I received.

I can understand why some reviewers have complained that the power and selected channel indicator LED's are too bright and are distracting. My solution was to put a 3.5 inch strip of gray electrical tape across the front of the unit. The gray is less obtrusive than the white electrical tape that I tried, and does it a better job of taming the LED's output. You get a diffuse lighted dot to indicate "power on" and the channel that is "on", and can neatly write the name of the signal for the channels on it [e.g. DVD, Fire Stick, Computer, Game, etc.] with a Ultra Fine Point permanent marker pen. Put a 3.5 inch strip of Scotch Magic Mending Tape on top to protect what you have written on the electrical tape if that is a concern.

18December2016 update -- one of the white LED's that indicates the selected channel has failed, but otherwise unit continues to work fine.

title: Lois good on the counter
text:
I’ve been using the Lois “Good on the Counter” set for about six weeks and overall I’m pleased with the purchase — it’s earned a solid 4 stars from me. I bought it primarily as a functional and attractive way to keep small kitchen items tidy on my countertop, and it delivers on both counts.

The design is simple and modern, which fits nicely with my mostly neutral kitchen. The materials feel sturdy; the weighted base keeps it from tipping when I reach for items, and the finish has held up well to daily use and occasional splashes. Assembly was minimal and straightforward — just a few pieces that snapped together — and the whole unit feels well-made rather than cheap.

Functionally, it’s great for organizing cooking utensils, a couple of fresh fruit, and the stray mail and shopping list that always seems to collect on the counter. The compartments are a good size: deep enough for spatulas and wooden spoons, but not so wide that it dominates the counter. I also appreciate the little non-slip pads on the bottom that protect the surface beneath.

Why not five stars? A couple of small issues. First, the paint finish has started to show faint scuffs where metal utensils rub against it — not a dealbreaker, but noticeable if you look closely. Second, while the size is perfect for my apartment kitchen, it might be a bit small for someone who wants a true catch-all for larger items or a big family’s cooking tools. Finally, the price felt a touch high compared to similar organizers I’ve seen, though the build quality somewhat justifies it.

In short, the Lois counter organizer is a stylish, practical addition to a mid-sized kitchen. It looks good, functions well, and will keep your everyday items within reach — just temper expectations if you need heavy-duty capacity.

title: excellent read
text: I rarely take the time to write reviews, but I felt compelled to do so after finishing this book. I picked it up on a whim during a rainy afternoon, expecting perhaps a lightweight weekend read that I would finish in a single sitting. I was completely wrong. This book demanded my full attention from the very first page and kept me engaged until the final word. It is rare to find a work that manages to be both intellectually stimulating and emotionally resonant at the same time, but the author has achieved something truly special here. The writing style is crisp and unpretentious, yet it carries a weight and depth that lingers in your mind long after you have closed the cover. I found myself pausing frequently to reflect on the themes presented, questioning my own assumptions and seeing the world through a slightly different lens. The characters were not merely vessels for the plot; they felt like real people with complex motivations, flaws, and dreams. You root for them, you despair for them, and you celebrate their victories as if they were your own. The pacing was impeccable. There were moments of high tension that kept me turning pages late into the night, balanced beautifully with quieter, more introspective scenes that allowed for breathing room and deeper connection. I appreciated that the author did not shy away from difficult topics, handling them with nuance and care. It is easy to write about life in the abstract, but it is much harder to capture the raw, messy reality of human experience with such authenticity and grace. This book does not offer easy answers or neat resolutions. Instead, it invites you to sit with the ambiguity and find meaning in the journey itself. For anyone who loves reading but feels like they have read everything, this is a reminder of why we love the medium in the first place. It is a story that matters. It is a story that stays with you. text:
I try really hard to not rehash the entire story or give a bunch of spoilers when I review a book, but it may be hard not to this time! I'll do my best, though. ;)

I received this book to rebiew from the Shut Up & Read group's Read It & Reap event. I have to say, I have been extremely fortunate in the books I've been given to review through them so far. There really haven't been any misses. :)

Anyway, about this book...

I admit it--halfway into the very first chapter I was convinced I was going to hate this book. Liora seemed like the typical, overly-angsty teenager often depicted in paranormal fantasy these days. I initially found her constant whiny and hating herself grating. All I can say is I'm so happy I read chapter 2!

Lucky kicks ass! There's really no other way to describe her. The demon half of Liora who takes over at night, separated from Liora by a curse, she is angry, obviously. And that anger is often turned toward Liora, her fully human side. She is also strong, practical, loyal to her friends, and more willing to look into herself and face the things that make her uncomfortable that she admits. And as time went by, I found Liora to be less annoying as she found her own strength and started to face her own inner "demons".

There are only a couple of things that prevented me from giving this book five stars. The first is that I felt like the romance between Keiran and Liora/Lucky felt too conveniently done to me. There didn't seem to be any build up to it at all. The second issue is that conversations sometimes felt stilted to me. While I appreciate that there was a distinct lack of inappropriate idioms throughout, the almost complete lack of contractions often made discussions feel too formal and unnatural.

This book had everything--romance, fear, growth, drama, excitement, sadness, and victory. It was a great story and I can't wait to read the next one!

title: Look What I See
text:
This series entitled, "Look What I See! Where Can I Be?" which includes the previous titles that explored "the neighborhood", "the home", "my animal friends" and "visiting China", now examines "the synagogue" with mixed results. The publisher promotes the book as "exploring a week in Jewish family life", but that week constitutes a rather confused timeline for most adults familiar with Jewish rituals and traditions. The concept is one that is completely appropriate for very young children. An inquisitive toddler and her doll view items relating to Jewish rituals and then, with a turn of the page, we see her and her family photographed at the larger event. For instance, the text reads, "On Sunday, I fell asleep in my stroller. When I woke up, I saw a Kiddish cup." First we view the Kiddish cup in a clear photo, and then the toddler asks, "Where was I? By the Chuppah at a wedding." Within the wedding photo, clever toddlers will notice an apple and also the doll in his stroller. These photos and questions and answers are repeated 7 times for the days of the week and make for an appealing, structured format. However, this format does not work as well in a synagogue as it probably does for "exploring the neighborhood". Confusion abounds as we are led to believe that Rosh Hashana and Simchat Torah fall within the same week, or that apples are an integral part of every Jewish ritual. Confusion continues as the reader assumes the text to be the words of the toddler ("I fell asleep in my stroller"), but the photo then matches what the plastic doll is doing rather than the young girl. Also, the plastic doll, with a droopy, oversized blue kippah, is generally unappealing. Another issue involves the choice of photographs of both people and ritual objects. For example, the lulav is cut off, the dancers are blurry, and the "menorah" they chose to display is the stylized, artistic synagogue wall version, which is certainly not something a toddler would recognize from the home version. This book may work for some families comfortable with Reform traditions, but, in general, it needs to be revamped to appeal to its intended audience of Jewish families with small children.

Reviewed by Lisa Silverman

I picked this book up largely based on the glowing descriptions in the catalog, hoping for a deep dive into the subject matter. Unfortunately, my experience with it was a mix of high hopes and eventual disappointment. The initial chapters are engaging enough, and the author has a pleasant writing style that makes the early pages flow smoothly. I found myself skimming through several chapters because the arguments felt repetitive and lacked the substantive evidence promised in the introduction. It is frustrating to invest time in a narrative that seems interested more in filling space than providing insight. For anyone looking for a comprehensive overview or a rigorous analysis, this title falls short. It stays surface-level for too long, missing the opportunity to offer a truly transformative perspective on the topic.

That said, it is not entirely without merit. If you are a casual reader who just wants something light to pass the time during a weekend, this might suffice. The layout is clean, and the font size is comfortable for long reading sessions. But if you are a serious student or enthusiast of the genre, you will likely feel let down by the lack of original thought and the reliance on clichéd conclusions. I expected more from the publisher given the hype surrounding the release. I would hesitate to recommend this to anyone seeking genuine intellectual stimulation. It feels like a cash-grab rather than a meaningful contribution to the field. There are better resources available for those who want to truly understand the nuances of this subject. title: Brlliant, funny, and even a bit disturbing
text:
"Dreams of the Rarebit Fiend" is McCay's overlooked masterpiece. "Little Nemo" gets all the press (and it deserves the highest possible praise) but The Fiend is often equally compelling. More adult in subject matter than Nemo, it is less visually resplendant, but still quite powerful in its invocation of the fears and hopes underlying our day-to-day thoughts.

This collection is the standard, but it collects only a fraction of what McCay produced (this is a reprint of a 1905 volume, but the strip ran until 1910 or 1911). You can pick up the Checker "Early Works" volumes for a more complete run (in questionable quality) and there are more strips in the Canemaker book on McCay as well as the Fantagraphics "Daydreams and Nightmares" (which I highly recommend).

Checker has since produced a fine collection: [[ASIN:1933160659 The Saturdays]] which would make a great follow-up to this book.

When I first wrote this review in 2006, I pleaded for someone to do this strip justice with a comprehensive reprint. Little did I know that Ulrich Merkl was, in fact, working on one at the time. You can search the web for his "The Complete Dream of the Rarebit Fiend" ([...]). I highly reccommend it, though it is a bit pricey. Amazon now lists it here: [[ASIN:3000207511 The Complete Dreams of the Rarebit Fiend]]

title: Unimpressed
text:
This looks like a fun puzzle. The concept is great. The execution? Not so much.

First of all, this puzzle, which is the size of two old 45 records stacked atop one another, arrives in a plastic package the size of your house.

Well, maybe not quite that big, but it is much, much larger than necessary. MUCH larger. So I was already not very happy with it. Then, I tried to open it, and made another discovery: if you for some reason need to perform emergency surgery in your home, the plastic encasing this puzzle will double as a scalpel.

Honestly, I think they just want you to buy it and put it on display in the box. This package is next to impossible to open.

And wasteful. Did I mention yet that this plastic package is much, much too big for it’s contents? Because it is.

Once I finally got the puzzle out, I mixed it up, spun it round, did the entire hokey-pokey. Then I started the process of solving it. I ordered the most challenging one since I am good at puzzles and wanted something that would tax my brain.

I am little, and have the hands to match. Even my childlike fingers had difficulty maneuvering the tiny inner rings. After about the fifth one from the center, it gets easier.

It took me under three minutes to solve. For the most difficult one. Counting the issues I had moving and turning the tiniest rings. Either I am some sort of prodigy, or this doesn’t deliver on the hours of fun puzzling promised. I tried the other side to see if it was a fluke. It was not. Nor is this like a Rubik’s Cube, where after you solve it, it’s fun to mix it up and try again. I haven’t had the urge to pick it up again after my initial tests, which I think says something.

Bottom line: extremely wasteful packaging containing a no-challenge “puzzle.” Maybe this would be better marketed as a fidget toy. Or to very small children. Would not recommend.
